# Enable your tokens in CCIP (Burn & Mint): Register from an EOA using Foundry
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry
Last Updated: 2025-10-30

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry (Burn & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat (Burn & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

In this tutorial you will:

1. Deploy a token on two chains using [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/).
2. Set up a `Burn Mint` token pool on each chain.
3. Configure and activate the pools in CCIP so your token becomes a Cross-Chain Token (CCT).
4. (Optional) Test the setup by minting and transferring tokens across networks.

<Aside type="note" title="If you do not explicitly configure these features, default behavior applies" />

## Before You Begin

<AnchoredAccordion title="How to configure deployment parameters?" number={2} depth={3}>
  Deployment parameters can be configured in two ways:

  1. Edit the `.json` files in `script/input/`.
  2. Pass environment variables inline at runtime.

  > **Note:** Environment variables take precedence over `.json` file values.

  #### Token Deployment Configuration

  Default values live in `script/input/token.json`:

  ```json filename="script/input/token.json"
  {
    "name": "BnM Test",
    "symbol": "BnM-T",
    "decimals": 18,
    "maxSupply": 0,
    "preMint": 0,
    "tokenAmountToMint": 1000000000000000000000,
    "tokenAmountToTransfer": 1000000000000000000
  }
  ```

  Deployment fields can be overridden with inline env vars:

  | Env var                    | Overrides (`token.json`) | Optional | Description                                                                                                  |
  | -------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `TOKEN_NAME`               | `.name`                  | Yes      | Token name                                                                                                   |
  | `TOKEN_SYMBOL`             | `.symbol`                | Yes      | Token symbol                                                                                                 |
  | `TOKEN_DECIMALS`           | `.decimals`              | Yes      | Decimal places (usually `18`)                                                                                |
  | `TOKEN_MAX_SUPPLY`         | `.maxSupply`             | Yes      | Max supply in smallest unit (`0` = unlimited)                                                                |
  | `TOKEN_PRE_MINT`           | `.preMint`               | Yes      | Amount pre-minted to the configured recipient (`0` = none)                                                   |
  | `TOKEN_PRE_MINT_RECIPIENT` | N/A (env-only)           | Yes      | Address receiving pre-minted tokens. If omitted and `TOKEN_PRE_MINT > 0`, the script defaults to broadcaster |
  | `CCIP_ADMIN_ADDRESS`       | N/A (env-only)           | Yes      | Address assigned as CCIP admin on the token. If omitted, broadcaster is used                                 |

  #### (Optional) Advanced Pool Hooks

  <Aside type="note" title="What are advanced pool hooks?">
    [Advanced Pool
    Hooks](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol)
    are an optional security layer you can attach to a token pool. They run checks:

    <ol>
      <li>**before** tokens are locked/burned (source chain)</li>
      <li>**before** tokens are released/minted (destination chain)</li>
    </ol>

    Most deployments do **not** need a hook. You would attach one only if you want to:

    <ul>
      <li>Make it so that only certain addresses can transfer your token cross-chain.</li>
      <li>Put in place additional checks for large transfers above a threshold amount.</li>
      <li>Plug in an external policy engine for custom compliance checks.</li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>

  Default values live in `script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json`:

  ```json filename="script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json"
  {
    "allowlist": [],
    "thresholdAmount": 0,
    "policyEngine": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "authorizedCallers": []
  }
  ```

  All fields can be overridden with inline env vars:

  | Env var              | Overrides (`advanced-pool-hooks.json`) | Optional | Description                                                                              |
  | -------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `ALLOWLIST`          | `.allowlist`                           | Yes      | Addresses allowed to transfer (CSV or JSON array)                                        |
  | `THRESHOLD_AMOUNT`   | `.thresholdAmount`                     | Yes      | Threshold amount after which additional hook checks/policy checks may apply (`0` = none) |
  | `POLICY_ENGINE`      | `.policyEngine`                        | Yes      | Policy engine contract address                                                           |
  | `AUTHORIZED_CALLERS` | `.authorizedCallers`                   | Yes      | Addresses authorized to call the hooks (CSV or JSON array)                               |

  > **Note:** A complete tutorial on setting up Advanced Pool Hooks can be found in our docs here: [Set advanced pool hooks using Foundry](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-foundry)
</AnchoredAccordion>

## Tutorial

### Prerequisites

<Aside type="caution" title="Before you continue" />

**Already have deployments? Skip only what you already have:**

- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, skip **Deploy Tokens**.
- If you have deployed tokens but not the corresponding pools, you must still run **Deploy Token Pools** before continuing.
- If you already have tokens and **V2-compatible** token pools deployed on **both** chains, skip both sections and move straight on to [Enablement](#enablement).

**If you already have a V1 token pool deployed and want to use newer features or prepare for lane migration:**

- You will need to deploy a **V2-compatible token pool**
- Your existing V1 pool can continue to support current transfers
- Follow the migration guide to upgrade your setup without disrupting your existing deployment

> **Read**: [Migrate from V1 to V2 token pools](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/migrate-from-v1-to-v2-burn-mint-foundry)

Before continuing, export the relevant addresses so subsequent scripts can find them:

```bash filename="Terminal"
export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_sepolia>
export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>

export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_sepolia>
export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>
```

<AnchoredAccordion title="(Optional) Configure Faster Than Finality for the Token Pool" number={4} depth={4}>
  1. CCIP 2.0 supports **faster than finality** as an opt-in feature, letting token issuers control the speed vs. security
     tradeoff for cross-chain transfers of their token.

  2. By default, a newly deployed token pool only allows transfers at default finality (equivalent to omitting `finality`
     or using `finality=finalized`).

  3. To enable faster than finality, the pool owner must configure which faster than finality modes are allowed. Senders then request
     one mode per transfer using `finality` (either `finality=finalized` or `finality=<N>` for block-depth faster than finality).

  > This section applies only to [**token pools with versions ≥ 2.0**](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/TokenPool.sol). Existing v1 pools do not support fast
  > finality.

  <Aside type="note" title="Pool-level finality vs. transaction-level finality">
    <ol>
      <li>
        <strong>Pool-level finality</strong> (allowed finality config): A setting the pool owner configures via{" "}
        <code>setAllowedFinalityConfig(bytes4)</code>.

        <ul>
          <li>
            Default = faster than finality is <strong>disabled</strong>. The pool only allows transfers that use default
            finality (omit <code>finality</code> or use <code>finality=finalized</code>).
          </li>

          <li>
            The pool can opt in to faster than finality by allowing a minimum block depth (<code>finality=\<N></code>
            ).
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>

      <li>
        <strong>Transaction-level finality</strong> (<code>finality</code>): A per-transfer setting the sender specifies
        via extra args when sending a CCIP message.

        <ul>
          <li>
            <code>finality=finalized</code> (or omit <code>finality</code>) = default finality. This is always allowed.
          </li>

          <li>
            <code>finality=\<N></code> = faster than finality using block depth (block confirmations). Only succeeds
            if the pool allows block-depth mode and the requested <code>N</code> is ≥ the pool's configured minimum.
          </li>
        </ul>

        Each transfer requests exactly <strong>one</strong> mode (either default finality or block depth).
      </li>
    </ol>

    Faster Than Finality transfers use the <strong>faster than finality</strong> rate limit bucket when configured. If the
    faster than finality bucket isn’t configured for a lane, the pool falls back to the standard rate limit bucket.
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="SetFinalityConfig.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/finality-config/SetFinalityConfig.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the pool configuration script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  BLOCK_DEPTH=32 \
    DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=1000000000000000000000 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=1000000000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/finality-config/SetFinalityConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

### Cross-chain Token Operations

If all the previous steps were successful, your CCT token is now fully registered and activated under the CCIP protocol.
Use these next steps to mint and transfer your tokens across networks.

<AnchoredAccordion title="Transfer Tokens Across Networks" number={2} depth={4}>
  Use the `ccip-cli` command to securely transfer tokens across networks from your terminal.
  Tokens will be:

  1. **burned** on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia), and,
  2. **minted** on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia). \\

  You can choose to pay CCIP fees using LINK tokens or the native gas token.

  > **Note:**
  >
  > 1. Add `--fee-token LINK` to pay CCIP fees in LINK. If you omit this flag, fees are paid in the native gas token.
  > 2. Use `--receiver <address>` for a custom recipient. If omitted on EVM-to-EVM, the receiver defaults to the sender.

  The CLI command expects the router address to be set in the environment variables. You can set it using the following command:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER=0x...
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Router address">
    You can find the router address for your chain in the [CCIP
    Directory](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/directory/testnet).
  </Aside>

  <Aside type="note" title="Token amounts in this tutorial">
    Earlier Foundry scripts use smallest-unit amounts (wei-like). In the <code>ccip-cli</code> examples below we use a
    compact, human-readable token amount (for example, <code>1.23</code>).
  </Aside>

  1. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia on **default finality**:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```

  2. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia using **faster than finality**:

  This assumes you enabled faster than finality on the pool in the optional finality configuration accordion above.
  When you pass <code>--extra finality=...</code>, <code>ccip-cli</code> encodes it into the CCIP message extra args.

  Transfer with explicit finalized finality (`finality=finalized`):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=finalized \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0xeee045c912703291e6d6166e4ef8bfb0a7fb9035af1a41ac00b65c58ad868a94 , messageId => 0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  ```

  Faster Than Finality using numeric block depth (`finality=<N>`):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=7 \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Understand Minimum Block Depth Requirements 🧑‍🏫">
    <ol>
      <li>
        The last command failed because the pool's <strong>allowed finality config</strong> requires a larger block depth
        for numeric faster than finality (for example, if you configured <code>BLOCK_DEPTH=32</code>) but we requested{" "}
        <code>finality=7</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        Try running the command again with an appropriate value for <code>finality</code> (for example,{" "}
        <code>--extra finality=20</code>), or omit <code>finality</code> to use default finality (
        <code>finality=finalized</code>).
      </li>

      <li>
        If you see a revert like <code>InvalidRequestedFinality(requestedFinality, allowedFinality)</code>, it means the
        requested mode (or depth) is not permitted by the pool.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

# Enable your tokens in CCIP (Burn & Mint): Register from an EOA using Hardhat
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-hardhat
Last Updated: 2026-04-24

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry (Burn & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat (Burn & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

In this tutorial you will:

1. Deploy a token on two chains using [Hardhat](https://hardhat.org/).
2. Set up a `Burn Mint` token pool on each chain.
3. Configure and activate the pools in CCIP so your token becomes a Cross-Chain Token (CCT).
4. (Optional) Test the setup by minting and transferring tokens across networks.

<Aside type="note" title="If you do not explicitly configure these features, default behavior applies" />

## Before You Begin

<AnchoredAccordion title="How to configure deployment parameters?" number={2} depth={3}>
  Deployment parameters can be configured in two ways:

  1. Edit the `.json` files in `input/`.
  2. Pass CLI flags inline at runtime.

  > **Note:** CLI flags take precedence over `.json` file values.

  #### Token Deployment Configuration

  Default values live in `input/token.json`:

  ```json filename="input/token.json"
  {
    "name": "BnM Test",
    "symbol": "BnM-T",
    "decimals": 18,
    "maxSupply": 0,
    "preMint": 0,
    "tokenAmountToMint": 1000000000000000000000,
    "tokenAmountToTransfer": 1000000000000000000
  }
  ```

  Deployment fields can be overridden with CLI flags:

  | Flag          | Overrides (`token.json`) | Description                                   |
  | ------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
  | `--name`      | `.name`                  | Token name                                    |
  | `--symbol`    | `.symbol`                | Token symbol                                  |
  | `--decimals`  | `.decimals`              | Decimal places (usually `18`)                 |
  | `--maxsupply` | `.maxSupply`             | Max supply in smallest unit (`0` = unlimited) |
  | `--premint`   | `.preMint`               | Amount pre-minted to deployer (`0` = none)    |

  #### (Optional) Advanced Pool Hooks

  <Aside type="note" title="What are advanced pool hooks?">
    [Advanced Pool
    Hooks](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol)
    are an optional security layer you can attach to a token pool. They run checks:

    <ol>
      <li>**before** tokens are locked/burned (source chain)</li>
      <li>**before** tokens are released/minted (destination chain)</li>
    </ol>

    Most deployments do **not** need a hook. You would attach one only if you want to:

    <ul>
      <li>Make it so that only certain addresses can transfer your token cross-chain.</li>
      <li>Put in place additional checks for large transfers above a threshold amount.</li>
      <li>Plug in an external policy engine for custom compliance checks.</li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>

  Default values live in `input/advanced-pool-hooks.json`:

  ```json filename="input/advanced-pool-hooks.json"
  {
    "allowlist": [],
    "thresholdAmount": 0,
    "policyEngine": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "authorizedCallers": []
  }
  ```

  All fields can be overridden with CLI flags:

  | Flag                  | Overrides (`advanced-pool-hooks.json`) | Description                                                                              |
  | --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `--allowlist`         | `.allowlist`                           | Addresses allowed to transfer (comma-separated)                                          |
  | `--thresholdamount`   | `.thresholdAmount`                     | Threshold amount after which additional hook checks/policy checks may apply (`0` = none) |
  | `--policyengine`      | `.policyEngine`                        | Policy engine contract address                                                           |
  | `--authorizedcallers` | `.authorizedCallers`                   | Addresses authorized to call the hooks (comma-separated)                                 |

  > **Note:** A complete tutorial on setting up Advanced Pool Hooks can be found in our docs here: [Set advanced pool hooks using Hardhat](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-hardhat)
</AnchoredAccordion>

## Tutorial

### Prerequisites

<Aside type="caution" title="Before you continue" />

**Already have deployments? Skip only what you already have:**

- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, skip **Deploy Tokens**.
- If you have deployed tokens but not the corresponding pools, you must still run **Deploy Token Pools** before continuing.
- If you already have tokens and **V2-compatible** token pools deployed on **both** chains, skip both sections and move straight on to [Enablement](#enablement).

**If you already have a V1 token pool deployed and want to use newer features or prepare for lane migration:**

- You will need to deploy a **V2-compatible token pool**
- Your existing V1 pool can continue to support current transfers
- Follow the migration guide to upgrade your setup without disrupting your existing deployment

> **Read**: [Migrate from V1 to V2 token pools](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/migrate-from-v1-to-v2-burn-mint-hardhat)

Before continuing, export the relevant addresses so subsequent tasks can find them:

```bash filename="Terminal"
# For tokens
export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_sepolia>
export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>

# For token pools
export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_sepolia>
export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>
```

<AnchoredAccordion title="Deploy Token Pools" number={2} depth={4}>

  A `BurnMintTokenPool` burns tokens on the source chain and mints the equivalent amount on the destination chain. For this to work, the pool must hold the token's mint and burn roles, which the task grants automatically after deployment.

### Enablement

<AnchoredAccordion title="(Optional) Configure Faster Than Finality for the Token Pool" number={4} depth={4}>
  1. CCIP 2.0 supports **faster than finality** as an opt-in feature, letting token issuers control the speed vs. security
     tradeoff for cross-chain transfers of their token.

  2. By default, a newly deployed token pool only allows transfers at default finality (equivalent to omitting `finality`
     or using `finality=finalized`).

  3. To enable faster than finality, the pool owner must configure which faster than finality modes are allowed. Senders then request
     one mode per transfer using `finality` (either `finality=finalized` or `finality=<N>` for block-depth faster than finality).

  > This section applies only to [**token pools with versions ≥ 2.0**](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/TokenPool.sol). Existing v1 pools do not support fast
  > finality.

  <Aside type="note" title="Pool-level finality vs. transaction-level finality">
    <ol>
      <li>
        <strong>Pool-level finality</strong> (allowed finality config): A setting the pool owner configures via{" "}
        <code>setAllowedFinalityConfig(bytes4)</code>.

        <ul>
          <li>
            Default = faster than finality is <strong>disabled</strong>. The pool only allows transfers that use default
            finality (omit <code>finality</code> or use <code>finality=finalized</code>).
          </li>

          <li>
            The pool can opt in to faster than finality by allowing a minimum block depth (<code>finality=\<N></code>
            ).
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>

      <li>
        <strong>Transaction-level finality</strong> (<code>finality</code>): A per-transfer setting the sender specifies
        via extra args when sending a CCIP message.

        <ul>
          <li>
            <code>finality=finalized</code> (or omit <code>finality</code>) = default finality. This is always allowed.
          </li>

          <li>
            <code>finality=\<N></code> = faster than finality using block depth (block confirmations). Only succeeds
            if the pool allows block-depth mode and the requested <code>N</code> is ≥ the pool's configured minimum.
          </li>
        </ul>

        Each transfer requests exactly <strong>one</strong> finality mode.
      </li>
    </ol>

    Faster Than Finality transfers use the <strong>faster than finality</strong> rate limit bucket when configured. If the
    faster than finality bucket isn’t configured for a lane, the pool falls back to the standard rate limit bucket.
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="setFinalityConfig.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/configure/finality-config/setFinalityConfig.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the pool configuration task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  # Allow block-depth faster than finality and optionally configure the faster than finality rate limit bucket
  npx hardhat setFinalityConfig \
    --blockdepth 32 \
    --destchain arbitrumSepolia \
    --outboundcapacity 1000000000000000000000 \
    --outboundrate 100000000000000000 \
    --inboundcapacity 1000000000000000000000 \
    --inboundrate 100000000000000000 \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  ========================================
  ⏱️  Set Finality Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Set finality config
  ========================================

    Current Finality Config: 0x00000014
    New Finality Config:     0x00000020
    Mode:                    BLOCK_DEPTH (32 blocks)

  ----------------------------------------
    Outbound [standard fallback]:
      Enabled:  true
      Capacity: 1000000000000000000000
      Rate:     100000000000000000
      Tokens:   1000000000000000000000
    Inbound [standard fallback]:
      Enabled:  true
      Capacity: 1000000000000000000000
      Rate:     100000000000000000
      Tokens:   1000000000000000000000

  [Step 1] Setting finality config on Ethereum Sepolia
  ⏳ Tx: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x280399cd3dce1815a30ca3763736c7cbc4a8018bdb3ba1b650e728479640f5b6
  ✅ Finality config set successfully!

  [Step 2] Updating rate limits (faster than finality bucket) on Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia
  New Configuration:
    Outbound Enabled:  true
    Outbound Capacity: 1000000000000000000000
    Outbound Rate:     100000000000000000
    Inbound Enabled:   true
    Inbound Capacity:  1000000000000000000000
    Inbound Rate:      100000000000000000

  ⏳ Tx: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0xa69245f229f41313d597ea452fa7c9d8ead9e05bfe36aad5a997a6850d198ac5
  ✅ Rate limits updated successfully!

  ----------------------------------------

  ----------------------------------------
    Outbound [faster than finality]:
      Enabled:  true

      Enabled:  true

  ========================================

  Finality Config: 0x00000020

  ```

### Cross-chain Token Operations

If all the previous steps were successful, your CCT token is now fully registered and activated under the CCIP protocol.
Use these next steps to mint and transfer your tokens across networks.

<AnchoredAccordion title="Transfer Tokens Across Networks" number={2} depth={4}>
  Use the `ccip-cli` command to securely transfer tokens across networks from your terminal.
  Tokens will be:

  1. **burned** on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia), and,
  2. **minted** on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia). \\

  You can choose to pay CCIP fees using LINK tokens or the native gas token.

  > **Note:**
  >
  > 1. Add `--fee-token LINK` to pay CCIP fees in LINK. If you omit this flag, fees are paid in the native gas token.
  > 2. Use `--receiver <address>` for a custom recipient. If omitted on EVM-to-EVM, the receiver defaults to the sender.

  The CLI command expects the router address to be set in the environment variables. You can set it using the following command:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER=0x...
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Router address">
    You can find the router address for your chain in the [CCIP
    Directory](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/directory/testnet).
  </Aside>

  1. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia on **default finality**:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="chainId vs. chainSelector">
    The <code>chainId</code> column shows the EVM chain ID (for example, <code>11155111</code> for Sepolia). The{" "}
    <code>chainSelector</code> is CCIP's own chain identifier used internally by the protocol. You do not need to set
    chain selectors yourself; the CLI and tasks resolve them automatically from the chain name.
  </Aside>

  2. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia using **faster than finality**:

  This assumes you enabled faster than finality on the pool in the optional finality configuration accordion above.
  When you pass <code>--extra finality=...</code>, <code>ccip-cli</code> encodes it into the CCIP message extra args.

  Transfer with explicit finalized finality (`finality=finalized`):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=finalized \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0xeee045c912703291e6d6166e4ef8bfb0a7fb9035af1a41ac00b65c58ad868a94 , messageId => 0x1dd7414db95d6c0f81e15780b93e3cda6df0c58fb32ff81a2c0468e952929264
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x1dd7414db95d6c0f81e15780b93e3cda6df0c58fb32ff81a2c0468e952929264
  ```

  Faster Than Finality using numeric block depth (`finality=<N>`):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=7 \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  error: Failed to call "ccipSend"
  Error = execution reverted: InvalidRequestedFinality(requestedFinality, allowedFinality)
  Revert.error = InvalidRequestedFinality(uint32 requestedFinality, uint32 allowedFinality)
  Revert.requestedFinality = 7n
  Revert.allowedFinality = 32n
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Understand Minimum Block Depth Requirements 🧑‍🏫">
    <ol>
      <li>
        The last command failed because the pool's <strong>allowed finality config</strong> requires a larger block depth
        for numeric faster than finality (for example, if you configured <code>--blockdepth 32</code>) but we requested{" "}
        <code>finality=7</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        Try running the command again with an appropriate value for <code>finality</code> (for example,{" "}
        <code>--extra finality=20</code>), or omit <code>finality</code> to use default finality (
        <code>finality=finalized</code>).
      </li>

      <li>
        If you see a revert like <code>InvalidRequestedFinality(requestedFinality, allowedFinality)</code>, it means the
        requested mode (or depth) is not permitted by the pool.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

# Enable your tokens in CCIP (Lock & Mint): Register from an EOA using Foundry
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry
Last Updated: 2025-10-30

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry (Lock & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat (Lock & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

In this tutorial you will:

1. Deploy a token on two chains using [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/).
2. Set up a `Lock & Release` token pool on the source chain and a `Burn Mint` token pool on the destination chain.
3. Configure and activate the pools in CCIP so your token becomes a Cross-Chain Token (CCT).
4. (Optional) Test the setup by minting and transferring tokens across networks.

<Aside type="note" title="If you do not explicitly configure these features, default behavior applies" />

## Before You Begin

<AnchoredAccordion title="How to configure deployment parameters?" number={2} depth={3}>
  Deployment parameters can be configured in two ways:

  1. Edit the `.json` files in `script/input/`.
  2. Pass environment variables inline at runtime.

  > **Note:** Environment variables take precedence over `.json` file values.

  #### Token Deployment Configuration

  Default values live in `script/input/token.json`:

  ```json filename="script/input/token.json"
  {
    "name": "BnM Test",
    "symbol": "BnM-T",
    "decimals": 18,
    "maxSupply": 0,
    "preMint": 0,
    "tokenAmountToMint": 1000000000000000000000,
    "tokenAmountToTransfer": 1000000000000000000
  }
  ```

  Deployment fields can be overridden with inline env vars:

  | Env var                                 | Overrides (`token.json`) | Optional | Description                                                                                                  |
  | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_NAME`</nobr>               | `.name`                  | Yes      | Token name                                                                                                   |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_SYMBOL`</nobr>             | `.symbol`                | Yes      | Token symbol                                                                                                 |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_DECIMALS`</nobr>           | `.decimals`              | Yes      | Decimal places (usually `18`)                                                                                |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_MAX_SUPPLY`</nobr>         | `.maxSupply`             | Yes      | Max supply in smallest unit (`0` = unlimited)                                                                |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_PRE_MINT`</nobr>           | `.preMint`               | Yes      | Amount pre-minted to the configured recipient (`0` = none)                                                   |
  | <nobr>`TOKEN_PRE_MINT_RECIPIENT`</nobr> | N/A (env-only)           | Yes      | Address receiving pre-minted tokens. If omitted and `TOKEN_PRE_MINT > 0`, the script defaults to broadcaster |
  | <nobr>`CCIP_ADMIN_ADDRESS`</nobr>       | N/A (env-only)           | Yes      | Address assigned as CCIP admin on the token. If omitted, broadcaster is used                                 |

  #### (Optional) Advanced Pool Hooks

  <Aside type="note" title="What are advanced pool hooks?">
    [Advanced Pool
    Hooks](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol)
    are an optional security layer you can attach to a token pool. They run checks:

    <ol>
      <li>**before** tokens are locked/burned (source chain)</li>
      <li>**before** tokens are released/minted (destination chain)</li>
    </ol>

    Most deployments do **not** need a hook. You would attach one only if you want to:

    <ul>
      <li>Make it so that only certain addresses can transfer your token cross-chain.</li>
      <li>Put in place additional checks for large transfers above a threshold amount.</li>
      <li>Plug in an external policy engine for custom compliance checks.</li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>

  Default values live in `script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json`:

  ```json filename="script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json"
  {
    "allowlist": [],
    "thresholdAmount": 0,
    "policyEngine": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "authorizedCallers": []
  }
  ```

  All fields can be overridden with inline env vars:

  | Env var                           | Overrides (`advanced-pool-hooks.json`) | Optional | Description                                                                              |
  | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`ALLOWLIST`</nobr>          | `.allowlist`                           | Yes      | Addresses allowed to transfer (CSV or JSON array)                                        |
  | <nobr>`THRESHOLD_AMOUNT`</nobr>   | `.thresholdAmount`                     | Yes      | Threshold amount after which additional hook checks/policy checks may apply (`0` = none) |
  | <nobr>`POLICY_ENGINE`</nobr>      | `.policyEngine`                        | Yes      | Policy engine contract address                                                           |
  | <nobr>`AUTHORIZED_CALLERS`</nobr> | `.authorizedCallers`                   | Yes      | Addresses authorized to call the hooks (CSV or JSON array)                               |

  > **Note:** A complete tutorial on setting up Advanced Pool Hooks can be found in our docs here: [Set advanced pool hooks using Foundry](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-foundry)
</AnchoredAccordion>

## Tutorial

### Prerequisites

<Aside type="caution" title="Before you continue" />

**Already have deployments? Skip only what you already have:**

- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, skip **Deploy Tokens**.
- If you have deployed tokens but not the corresponding pools and lockbox, you must still run **Deploy Token Pools** before continuing.
- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, **V2-compatible** token pools deployed on **both** chains, and the lockbox deployed on the **Lock & Release** side (Ethereum Sepolia), skip both sections and move straight on to [Enablement](#enablement).

**If you already have a V1 token pool deployed and want to use newer features or prepare for lane migration:**

- You will need to deploy a **V2-compatible token pool**
- Your existing V1 pool can continue to support current transfers
- Follow the migration guide to upgrade your setup without disrupting your existing deployment

> **Read**: [Migrate from V1 to V2 token pools](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/migrate-from-v1-to-v2-lock-mint-foundry)

Before continuing, export the relevant addresses so subsequent scripts can find them:

```bash filename="Terminal"
export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_sepolia>
export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>

export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_sepolia>
export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>
```

<AnchoredAccordion title="Deploy Token Pools" number={2} depth={4}>
  This tutorial deploys:

  - A Lock & Release token pool on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia)
  - A Burn & Mint token pool on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia)
  - An `ERC20LockBox` to hold token liquidity on behalf of the Lock & Release token pool on the source chain.
  - On the destination chain, the tokens are simply burned or minted as required by the Burn & Mint token pool.

  <Aside type="note" title="Note">
    These scripts deploy `V2` token pools that unlock new features as part of CCIP 2.0. Check out how to use these new
    features in the following sections.
  </Aside>

  ##### Deploy ERC20LockBox (Ethereum Sepolia)

  The [`ERC20LockBox`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/ERC20LockBox.sol) holds token liquidity on behalf of the [`LockReleaseTokenPool`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/LockReleaseTokenPool.sol). It must be deployed before the pool.

  <GitHubCard title="DeployERC20LockBox.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/deploy/DeployERC20LockBox.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the lockbox deployment script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Deploy the ERC20LockBox on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  forge script \
    script/deploy/DeployERC20LockBox.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast \
    --verify
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  📦 Deploy ERC20 LockBox
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Action:       Deploy ERC20 lockbox
  ========================================

  ERC20LockBox Parameters:
  Token:                        0x9602399103Ff5F87587Ac5A28E1551A0bA0c6C0D
  Authorized Callers:           None (add after deploying the token pool)

  [Step 1] Deploying ERC20LockBox on Ethereum Sepolia
  ERC20LockBox deployed at: 0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  ✅ ERC20LockBox deployed successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Deployment Complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  ERC20LockBox Address: 0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b

  Copy this address to use in the next commands:
  LOCK_BOX=0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  ========================================
  ```

  After deployment, the lockbox address is automatically saved to:

  ```bash
  script/deployments/lock-boxes/{CHAIN_NAME_IDENTIFIER}/{timestamp}-{SYMBOL}-LockBox.json
  ```

  2. Set the environment variable for the deployed lockbox address:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export LOCK_BOX=0x...
  ```

  ##### Deploy Lock & Release Token Pool (Ethereum Sepolia)

  Use this script to [deploy a Lock & Release token pool](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/LockReleaseTokenPool.sol) on the source chain. A `LockReleaseTokenPool` locks tokens in the `ERC20LockBox` on the source chain during outbound transfers and releases escrowed tokens during inbound transfers.

  <GitHubCard title="DeployLockReleaseTokenPool.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/deploy/DeployLockReleaseTokenPool.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the Lock & Release token pool deployment script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Deploy a Lock & Release token pool for the deployed token on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  LOCK_BOX=$LOCK_BOX \
    forge script \
    script/deploy/DeployLockReleaseTokenPool.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast \
    --verify
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"

  ========================================

  Action:       Deploy lock & release token pool

  RMN Proxy:                    0xba3f6251de62dED61Ff98590cB2fDf6871FbB991
  LockBox:                      0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  AdvancedPoolHooks:            None (0x0)
  ```

  After deployment, the pool address is automatically saved to:

  ```bash
  script/deployments/token-pools/{CHAIN_NAME_IDENTIFIER}/{timestamp}-{SYMBOL}-LockReleaseTokenPool.json
  ```

  2. Set the environment variable for the deployed pool address:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  ```

  ##### Authorize Pool on LockBox (Ethereum Sepolia)

  The pool must be authorized as a caller on the lockbox before it can deposit and withdraw tokens during cross-chain transfers.

  <GitHubCard title="UpdateAuthorizedCallers.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/authorized-callers/UpdateAuthorizedCallers.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the authorized callers script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Authorize the token pool on the lockbox:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  LOCK_BOX=$LOCK_BOX \
    ADD_ADDRESSES=$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL \
    forge script \
    script/configure/authorized-callers/UpdateAuthorizedCallers.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================

  ========================================

  LockBox:      0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b

  [0] 0x8a1b2C3d4E5F60718293a4B5c6D7E8F901234567

  ========================================

  ========================================

  LockBox:      https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x1c0b9A8f7E6d5C4b3A2f1E0d9C8b7A6f5E4d3C2b
  ========================================
  ```

  ##### Deploy Burn & Mint Token Pool (Arbitrum Sepolia)

  Use this script to [deploy a Burn & Mint token pool](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/BurnMintTokenPool.sol) on the destination chain. A `BurnMintTokenPool` burns tokens on the source chain and mints the equivalent amount on the destination chain, so the pool must hold the destination token's mint and burn roles, which the script grants automatically after deployment.

  <GitHubCard title="DeployBurnMintTokenPool.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/deploy/DeployBurnMintTokenPool.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the Burn & Mint token pool deployment script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Deploy a Burn & Mint token pool for the deployed token on Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  forge script \
    script/deploy/DeployBurnMintTokenPool.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast \
    --verify
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔥⚒️ Deploy Burn & Mint Token Pool
  ========================================
  Chain:        Arbitrum Sepolia
  Action:       Deploy burn & mint token pool
  ========================================

  Token Pool Parameters:
  Token:                        0x5B3c8F2a9D4e7A1c6F0b3E8d5C9a2F4b7D1e6A3c
  Decimals:                     18
  Router:                       0x2a9C5afB0d0e4BAb2BCdaE109EC4b0c4Be15a165
  RMN Proxy:                    0x9527E2d01A3064ef6b50c1Da1C0cC523803BCFF2
  AdvancedPoolHooks:            None (0x0)

  [Step 1] Deploying BurnMintTokenPool on Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool deployed at: 0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  https://sepolia.arbiscan.io/address/0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d

  ```

  After deployment, the pool address is automatically saved to:

  ```bash
  script/deployments/token-pools/{CHAIN_NAME_IDENTIFIER}/{timestamp}-{SYMBOL}-BurnMintTokenPool.json
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Token role-grant fallback">
    <ol>
      <li>
        The script attempts to call <code>grantMintAndBurnRoles</code> on the token to grant the pool mint and burn
        rights.
      </li>

      <li>If the token does not implement this function, the script prints instructions to grant the roles manually.</li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  ##### Set environment variables

  Set the environment variables for the deployed token pool addresses:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  ```
</AnchoredAccordion>

### Enablement

These steps configure your token pools and activate them under the CCIP protocol so your token becomes a fully registered Cross-Chain Token (CCT).

<AnchoredAccordion title="Accept Admin Role" number={2} depth={4}>

  <GitHubCard title="AcceptAdminRole.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/setup/AcceptAdminRole.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">

<AnchoredAccordion title="(Optional) Configure Faster Than Finality for the Token Pool" number={4} depth={4} anchorId="optional-configure-fast-finality-for-the-token-pool">
  1. CCIP 2.0 supports **faster than finality** as an opt-in feature, letting token issuers control the speed vs. security
     tradeoff for cross-chain transfers of their token.

  2. By default, a newly deployed token pool only allows transfers at default finality (equivalent to omitting `finality`
     or using `finality=finalized`).

  3. To enable faster than finality, the pool owner must configure which faster than finality modes are allowed. Senders then request
     faster than finality per transfer using a numeric block depth via `finality=<N>` (minimum recommended depth: `32`).

  > This section applies only to [**token pools with versions ≥ 2.0**](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/TokenPool.sol). Existing v1 pools do not support fast
  > finality.
  >
  > In this tutorial, configure faster than finality on both token pools: the `Lock & Release` pool on Ethereum Sepolia and the
  > `Burn Mint` pool on Arbitrum Sepolia.

  <Aside type="note" title="Pool-level finality vs. transaction-level finality">
    <ol>
      <li>
        <strong>Pool-level finality</strong> (allowed finality config): A setting the pool owner configures via{" "}
        <code>setAllowedFinalityConfig(bytes4)</code>.

        <ul>
          <li>
            Default = faster than finality is <strong>disabled</strong>. The pool only allows transfers that use default
            finality (omit <code>finality</code> or use <code>finality=finalized</code>).
          </li>

          <li>
            The pool can opt in to faster than finality by allowing a minimum block depth (<code>finality=\<N></code>
            ).
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>

      <li>
        <strong>Transaction-level finality</strong> (<code>finality</code>): A per-transfer setting the sender specifies
        via extra args when sending a CCIP message.

        <ul>
          <li>
            <code>finality=finalized</code> (or omit <code>finality</code>) = default finality. This is always allowed.
          </li>

          <li>
            <code>finality=\<N></code> = faster than finality using block depth (block confirmations). Only succeeds
            if the pool allows block-depth mode and the requested <code>N</code> is ≥ the pool's configured minimum.
          </li>
        </ul>

        Each transfer uses either default finality or block depth.
      </li>
    </ol>

    Faster Than Finality transfers use the <strong>faster than finality</strong> rate limit bucket when configured. If the
    faster than finality bucket isn’t configured for a lane, the pool falls back to the standard rate limit bucket.
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="SetFinalityConfig.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/finality-config/SetFinalityConfig.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the pool configuration script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  BLOCK_DEPTH=32 \
    DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=1000000000000000000000 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=1000000000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/finality-config/SetFinalityConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  ⏱️  Set Finality Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia

  New Finality Config:          0x00000020

  ✅ Finality config set successfully!

  ========================================

  ========================================
  ```

  2. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  BLOCK_DEPTH=32 \
    DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA \
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

</AnchoredAccordion>

### Cross-chain Token Operations

If all the previous steps were successful, your CCT token is now fully registered and activated under the CCIP protocol.
Use these next steps to mint and transfer your tokens across networks.

<AnchoredAccordion title="Transfer Tokens Across Networks" number={2} depth={4}>
  Use the `ccip-cli` command to securely transfer tokens across networks from your terminal.
  Tokens will be:

  1. **locked** on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia), and,
  2. **minted** on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia). \\

  You can choose to pay CCIP fees using LINK tokens or the native gas token.

  > **Note:**
  >
  > 1. Add `--fee-token LINK` to pay CCIP fees in LINK. If you omit this flag, fees are paid in the native gas token.
  > 2. Use `--receiver <address>` for a custom recipient. If omitted on EVM-to-EVM, the receiver defaults to the sender.

  The CLI command expects the router address to be set in the environment variables. You can set it using the following command:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER=0x...
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Router address">
    You can find the router address for your chain in the [CCIP
    Directory](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/directory/testnet).
  </Aside>

  <Aside type="note" title="Token amounts in this tutorial">
    Earlier Foundry scripts use smallest-unit amounts (wei-like). In the <code>ccip-cli</code> examples below we use a
    compact, human-readable token amount (for example, <code>1.23</code>).
  </Aside>

  1. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia on **default finality**:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```

  2. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia using **faster than finality (block depth)**:

  This assumes you enabled faster than finality on the pool in the optional finality configuration accordion above.
  When you pass <code>--extra finality=...</code>, <code>ccip-cli</code> encodes it into the CCIP message extra args.

  Faster Than Finality using numeric block depth (`finality=<N>`). Use a value of at least `32`:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=32 \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0xeee045c912703291e6d6166e4ef8bfb0a7fb9035af1a41ac00b65c58ad868a94 , messageId => 0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Understand Minimum Block Depth Requirements 🧑‍🏫">
    <ol>
      <li>
        If a transfer reverts with <code>InvalidRequestedFinality(requestedFinality, allowedFinality)</code>, it usually
        means the pool requires a larger block depth than you requested (for example, the pool minimum is <code>32</code>{" "}
        but you requested a smaller value).
      </li>

      <li>
        Use a value of at least <code>32</code> (for example, <code>--extra finality=32</code>), or omit{" "}
        <code>finality</code> for default finality.
      </li>

      <li>Other reverts may indicate the requested depth (or mode) is not permitted by the pool.</li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

# Enable your tokens in CCIP (Lock & Mint): Register from an EOA using Hardhat
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-hardhat
Last Updated: 2026-04-24

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry (Lock & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat (Lock & Mint)",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

In this tutorial you will:

1. Deploy a token on two chains using [Hardhat](https://hardhat.org/).
2. Set up a `Lock & Release` token pool on the source chain and a `Burn Mint` token pool on the destination chain.
3. Configure and activate the pools in CCIP so your token becomes a Cross-Chain Token (CCT).
4. (Optional) Test the setup by minting and transferring tokens across networks.

<Aside type="note" title="If you do not explicitly configure these features, default behavior applies" />

## Before You Begin

<AnchoredAccordion title="How to configure deployment parameters?" number={2} depth={3}>
  Deployment parameters can be configured in two ways:

  1. Edit the `.json` files in `input/`.
  2. Pass CLI flags inline at runtime.

  > **Note:** CLI flags take precedence over `.json` file values.

  #### Token Deployment Configuration

  Default values live in `input/token.json`:

  ```json filename="input/token.json"
  {
    "name": "BnM Test",
    "symbol": "BnM-T",
    "decimals": 18,
    "maxSupply": 0,
    "preMint": 0,
    "tokenAmountToMint": 1000000000000000000000,
    "tokenAmountToTransfer": 1000000000000000000
  }
  ```

  Deployment fields can be overridden with CLI flags:

  | Flag                       | Overrides (`token.json`) | Description                                   |
  | -------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`--name`</nobr>      | `.name`                  | Token name                                    |
  | <nobr>`--symbol`</nobr>    | `.symbol`                | Token symbol                                  |
  | <nobr>`--decimals`</nobr>  | `.decimals`              | Decimal places (usually `18`)                 |
  | <nobr>`--maxsupply`</nobr> | `.maxSupply`             | Max supply in smallest unit (`0` = unlimited) |
  | <nobr>`--premint`</nobr>   | `.preMint`               | Amount pre-minted to deployer (`0` = none)    |

  #### (Optional) Advanced Pool Hooks

  <Aside type="note" title="What are advanced pool hooks?">
    [Advanced Pool
    Hooks](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol)
    are an optional security layer you can attach to a token pool. They run checks:

    <ol>
      <li>**before** tokens are locked/burned (source chain)</li>
      <li>**before** tokens are released/minted (destination chain)</li>
    </ol>

    Most deployments do **not** need a hook. You would attach one only if you want to:

    <ul>
      <li>Make it so that only certain addresses can transfer your token cross-chain.</li>
      <li>Put in place additional checks for large transfers above a threshold amount.</li>
      <li>Plug in an external policy engine for custom compliance checks.</li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>

  Default values live in `input/advanced-pool-hooks.json`:

  ```json filename="input/advanced-pool-hooks.json"
  {
    "allowlist": [],
    "thresholdAmount": 0,
    "policyEngine": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "authorizedCallers": []
  }
  ```

  All fields can be overridden with CLI flags:

  | Flag                               | Overrides (`advanced-pool-hooks.json`) | Description                                                                              |
  | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`--allowlist`</nobr>         | `.allowlist`                           | Addresses allowed to transfer (comma-separated)                                          |
  | <nobr>`--thresholdamount`</nobr>   | `.thresholdAmount`                     | Threshold amount after which additional hook checks/policy checks may apply (`0` = none) |
  | <nobr>`--policyengine`</nobr>      | `.policyEngine`                        | Policy engine contract address                                                           |
  | <nobr>`--authorizedcallers`</nobr> | `.authorizedCallers`                   | Addresses authorized to call the hooks (comma-separated)                                 |

  > **Note:** A complete tutorial on setting up Advanced Pool Hooks can be found in our docs here: [Set advanced pool hooks using Hardhat](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-hardhat)
</AnchoredAccordion>

## Tutorial

### Prerequisites

<Aside type="caution" title="Before you continue" />

**Already have deployments? Skip only what you already have:**

- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, skip **Deploy Tokens**.
- If you have deployed tokens but not the corresponding pools and lockbox, you must still run **Deploy Token Pools** before continuing.
- If you already have tokens deployed on **both** chains, **V2-compatible** token pools deployed on **both** chains, and the lockbox deployed on the **Lock & Release** side (Ethereum Sepolia), skip both sections and move straight on to [Enablement](#enablement).

**If you already have a V1 token pool deployed and want to use newer features or prepare for lane migration:**

- You will need to deploy a **V2-compatible token pool**
- Your existing V1 pool can continue to support current transfers
- Follow the migration guide to upgrade your setup without disrupting your existing deployment

> **Read**: [Migrate from V1 to V2 token pools](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/migrate-from-v1-to-v2-lock-mint-foundry)

Before continuing, export the relevant addresses so subsequent tasks can find them:

```bash filename="Terminal"
export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_sepolia>
export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=<your_token_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>

export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_sepolia>
export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=<your_token_pool_address_on_arbitrum_sepolia>
```

<AnchoredAccordion title="Deploy Token Pools" number={2} depth={4}>
  This tutorial deploys:

  - A Lock & Release token pool on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia)
  - A Burn & Mint token pool on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia)
  - An `ERC20LockBox` to hold token liquidity on behalf of the Lock & Release token pool on the source chain.
  - On the destination chain, the tokens are simply burnt or minted as required by the Burn & Mint token pool.

  <Aside type="note" title="Note">
    These tasks deploy `V2` token pools that unlock new features as part of CCIP 2.0. Check out how to use these new
    features in the following sections.
  </Aside>

  ##### Deploy ERC20LockBox (Ethereum Sepolia)

  The [`ERC20LockBox`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/ERC20LockBox.sol) holds token liquidity on behalf of the [`LockReleaseTokenPool`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/LockReleaseTokenPool.sol). It must be deployed before the pool.

  <GitHubCard title="deployERC20LockBox.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/deploy/deployERC20LockBox.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">

  </GitHubCard>


### Enablement

These steps configure your token pools and activate them under the CCIP protocol so your token becomes a truly Cross-Chain Token (CCT).

<AnchoredAccordion title="(Optional) Configure Faster Than Finality for the Token Pool" number={4} depth={4} anchorId="optional-configure-fast-finality-for-the-token-pool">
  1. CCIP 2.0 supports **faster than finality** as an opt-in feature, letting token issuers control the speed vs. security
     tradeoff for cross-chain transfers of their token.

  2. By default, a newly deployed token pool only allows transfers at default finality (equivalent to omitting `finality`
     or using `finality=finalized`).

  3. To enable faster than finality, the pool owner must configure which faster than finality modes are allowed. Senders then request
     faster than finality per transfer using a numeric block depth via `finality=<N>` (minimum recommended depth: `32`).

  > This section applies only to [**token pools with versions ≥ 2.0**](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/TokenPool.sol). Existing v1 pools do not support fast
  > finality.
  >
  > In this tutorial, configure faster than finality on both token pools: the `Lock & Release` pool on Ethereum Sepolia and the
  > `Burn Mint` pool on Arbitrum Sepolia.

  <Aside type="note" title="Pool-level finality vs. transaction-level finality">
    <ol>
      <li>
        <strong>Pool-level finality</strong> (allowed finality config): A setting the pool owner configures via{" "}
        <code>setAllowedFinalityConfig(bytes4)</code>.

        <ul>
          <li>
            Default = faster than finality is <strong>disabled</strong>. The pool only allows transfers that use default
            finality (omit <code>finality</code> or use <code>finality=finalized</code>).
          </li>

          <li>
            The pool can opt in to faster than finality by allowing a minimum block depth (<code>finality=\<N></code>
            ).
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>

      <li>
        <strong>Transaction-level finality</strong> (<code>finality</code>): A per-transfer setting the sender specifies
        via extra args when sending a CCIP message.

        <ul>
          <li>
            <code>finality=finalized</code> (or omit <code>finality</code>) = default finality. This is always allowed.
          </li>

          <li>
            <code>finality=\<N></code> = faster than finality using block depth (block confirmations). Only succeeds
            if the pool allows block-depth mode and the requested <code>N</code> is ≥ the pool's configured minimum.
          </li>
        </ul>

        Each transfer uses either default finality or block depth.
      </li>
    </ol>

    Faster Than Finality transfers use the <strong>faster than finality</strong> rate limit bucket when configured. If the
    faster than finality bucket isn’t configured for a lane, the pool falls back to the standard rate limit bucket.
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="setFinalityConfig.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/configure/finality-config/setFinalityConfig.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the pool configuration task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  1. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat setFinalityConfig \
    --blockdepth 32 \
    --destchain arbitrumSepolia \
    --outboundcapacity 1000000000000000000000 \
    --outboundrate 100000000000000000 \
    --inboundcapacity 1000000000000000000000 \
    --inboundrate 100000000000000000 \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"

  ```

  2. Set the allowed finality config for the token pool on Arbitrum Sepolia:


### Cross-chain Token Operations

If all the previous steps were successful, your CCT token is now fully registered and activated under the CCIP protocol.
Use these next steps to mint and transfer your tokens across networks.

<AnchoredAccordion title="Transfer Tokens Across Networks" number={2} depth={4}>
  Use the `ccip-cli` command to securely transfer tokens across networks from your terminal.
  Tokens will be:

  1. **locked** on the source chain (Ethereum Sepolia), and,
  2. **minted** on the destination chain (Arbitrum Sepolia). \\

  You can choose to pay CCIP fees using LINK tokens or the native gas token.

  > **Note:**
  >
  > 1. Add `--fee-token LINK` to pay CCIP fees in LINK. If you omit this flag, fees are paid in the native gas token.
  > 2. Use `--receiver <address>` for a custom recipient. If omitted on EVM-to-EVM, the receiver defaults to the sender.

  The CLI command expects the router address to be set in the environment variables. You can set it using the following command:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER=0x...
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Router address">
    You can find the router address for your chain in the [CCIP
    Directory](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/directory/testnet).
  </Aside>

  <Aside type="note" title="Token amounts in this tutorial">
    Earlier Hardhat tasks use smallest-unit amounts (wei-like). In the <code>ccip-cli</code> examples below we use a
    compact, human-readable token amount (for example, <code>1.23</code>).
  </Aside>

  1. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia on **default finality**:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```

  2. Transfer tokens from Ethereum Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia using **faster than finality (block depth)**:

  This assumes you enabled faster than finality on the pool in the optional finality configuration accordion above.
  When you pass <code>--extra finality=...</code>, <code>ccip-cli</code> encodes it into the CCIP message extra args.

  Faster Than Finality using numeric block depth (`finality=<N>`). Use a value of at least `32`:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourReceiverAddress \
    --extra finality=32 \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0xeee045c912703291e6d6166e4ef8bfb0a7fb9035af1a41ac00b65c58ad868a94 , messageId => 0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Understand Minimum Block Depth Requirements 🧑‍🏫">
    <ol>
      <li>
        If a transfer reverts with <code>InvalidRequestedFinality(requestedFinality, allowedFinality)</code>, it usually
        means the pool requires a larger block depth than you requested (for example, the pool minimum is <code>32</code>{" "}
        but you requested a smaller value).
      </li>

      <li>
        Use a value of at least <code>32</code> (for example, <code>--extra finality=32</code>), or omit{" "}
        <code>finality</code> for default finality.
      </li>

      <li>Other reverts may indicate the requested depth (or mode) is not permitted by the pool.</li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>
