# Set advanced pool hooks using Foundry
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-foundry
Last Updated: 2026-05-05

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

CCIP v2 token pools support an optional [`AdvancedPoolHooks`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol) contract being attached to them. \
This contract can run certain checks :

1. before tokens are locked/burned (source chain)
2. before tokens are released/minted (destination chain)

If no hooks contract is attached, the token pool keeps its existing behavior.

Hooks are enforced only when **both** of these aspects are configured:

- The token pool points to the `AdvancedPoolHooks` contract.
- The hooks contract authorizes that token pool as a caller.

Authorize the pool before attaching hooks so the first hook call does not revert. Hooks are configured **per token pool, per chain**, which means that:
you need to repeat this setup for any other pool where you want hooks enforced.

> **Note:** Remember. Your CCT token can be deployed on multiple chains, with each chain having its own token pool.

In this tutorial you will:

1. Review the current hooks state on your deployed token pool.
2. Send a baseline transfer (*with no hooks attached*). This should succeed.
3. Deploy an `AdvancedPoolHooks` contract with your deployer address on the allowlist.
4. Authorize the pool as a caller on the hooks contract and attach the hooks contract to the token pool.
5. Verify the hooks attachment, authorized callers, and allowlist state.
6. Remove your address from the allowlist.
7. Attempt a transfer (*expected to revert with `SenderNotAllowed(address)`*).
8. Detach the hooks contract.
9. Send a transfer again (*expected to succeed*).
10. Manage the allowlist over time (add, remove, and check addresses).

## Before You Begin

## Tutorial

<AnchoredAccordion title="Review current pool hooks state" number={2} depth={3}>
  Use the `GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol` script to check whether an `AdvancedPoolHooks` contract is currently attached to your token pool.

  <GitHubCard title="GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/allowlist/GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the hooks query script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  forge script \
    script/configure/allowlist/GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Example output (no hooks attached):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🪝 Get Advanced Pool Hooks
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View pool hooks
  ========================================

  No AdvancedPoolHooks contract is attached to this pool.
  Deploy one with DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol and attach it via UpdateAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol.

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  <Aside type="note">
    1. <code>getAdvancedPoolHooks()</code> is only available on TokenPool v2.0 and later. If the script reverts with a
       missing function selector, the pool is a v1 contract and does not support hooks. 2. If your token pool already has
       hooks attached, you can detach them by following the 'Detach hooks' section, to follow the tutorial.
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Deploy AdvancedPoolHooks" number={4} depth={3}>
  Use the `DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol` script to deploy a new hooks contract.

  <Aside type="note" title="Inspect script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json before deployment">
    The <code>DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol</code> script reads <code>script/input/advanced-pool-hooks.json</code> when
    environment variables are omitted. Inspect the file and clear any stale addresses you do not intend to use. Because
    allowlist enablement is permanent, prefer setting <code>ALLOWLIST</code> and <code>AUTHORIZED_CALLERS</code>{" "}
    explicitly.
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/allowlist/DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the hooks deployment script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  Deployment inputs:

  - `ALLOWLIST`: CSV or JSON array of original outbound sender addresses allowed to initiate outbound transfers.
  - `AUTHORIZED_CALLERS`: CSV or JSON array of token pool addresses permitted to invoke the hooks.

  <Aside type="caution" title="Allowlist enablement is permanent">
    <ol>
      <li>
        Allowlist mode is set at deployment time and <strong>cannot be changed later</strong>.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you deploy with a non-empty <code>ALLOWLIST</code>, the allowlist is permanently enabled.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you deploy with an empty allowlist, calling <code>applyAllowListUpdates()</code> later will revert with{" "}
        <code>AllowListNotEnabled()</code>.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  In this example, you will deploy hooks on Ethereum Sepolia with your deployer address on the allowlist, and authorize your token pool as a caller:

  <Aside type="note" title="Why we start by allowlisting the deployer">
    1. You will first allowlist your deployer address so you can attach hooks without immediately blocking your own
       transfers. 2. Later in the tutorial, you will remove your address from the allowlist to demonstrate an enforced
       failure.
  </Aside>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ALLOWLIST=0xYourDeployerAddress \
  AUTHORIZED_CALLERS=$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL \
  forge script \
  script/configure/allowlist/DeployAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol \
  --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
  --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
  --broadcast \
  --verify
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔒 Deploy Advanced Pool Hooks
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Action:       Deploy pool hooks
  ========================================

  Advanced Pool Hooks Parameters:
  Allowlist Enabled:            Yes
  Allowlist Size:               1
  [0] 0x3A34637a41aB08519d30Fdb65344aBa8E9b2e994
  Threshold Amount:             Disabled (0)
  Policy Engine:                Disabled (0x0)
  Authorized Callers Enabled:   Yes
  Authorized Callers Size:      1
  [0] 0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9

  [Step 1] Deploying AdvancedPoolHooks on Ethereum Sepolia
  AdvancedPoolHooks deployed at: 0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE
  https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE
  ✅ AdvancedPoolHooks deployed successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Deployment Complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  AdvancedPoolHooks Address: 0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE
  https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE

  Deployment saved: script/deployments/advanced-pool-hooks/ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA/1746652800-AdvancedPoolHooks.json

  Configuration Summary:
  Allowlist:                    Enabled
  Threshold:                    Disabled
  Policy Engine:                Disabled
  Authorized Callers:           Enabled

  Next Steps:
  1. When deploying a TokenPool, pass this hooks address as the 'poolHooks' parameter
  2. Attach to an existing pool: TOKEN_POOL=<address> NEW_HOOK=<address> forge script script/configure/allowlist/UpdateAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol --rpc-url $RPC_URL --account $KEYSTORE_NAME --broadcast
  3. Manage allowlist: POOL_HOOKS=<address> ADD_ADDRESSES="0xAddr" forge script script/configure/allowlist/UpdateAllowList.s.sol --rpc-url $RPC_URL --account $KEYSTORE_NAME --broadcast
  ========================================
  ```

  Export the hooks address for subsequent commands:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export POOL_HOOKS=0xHooksAddress
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Deployment address recovery">
    <ul>
      <li>
        Deployment addresses are saved to <code>script/deployments/advanced-pool-hooks/</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you lose the session export, retrieve the address from the JSON file under the <code>POOL_HOOKS</code> key.
      </li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Verify the setup" number={6} depth={3}>
  Run the following read-only scripts to verify wiring. These checks confirm configuration state only;the next step attempts a transfer that is expected to revert.

  **1. Confirm hooks are attached to the pool:**

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  forge script \
    script/configure/allowlist/GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Expected output should now show your hooks address:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"

  ========================================

     0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE

  ========================================
  ```

  **2. Confirm the pool is an authorized caller on the hooks:**

  <GitHubCard title="GetAuthorizedCallers.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/authorized-callers/GetAuthorizedCallers.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">

  </GitHubCard>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  POOL_HOOKS=$POOL_HOOKS \

  ```

  Your output should look something like this:


  **3. View the current allowlist:**

  <GitHubCard title="GetAllowList.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/allowlist/GetAllowList.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the allowlist query script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  POOL_HOOKS=$POOL_HOOKS \
    forge script \
    script/configure/allowlist/GetAllowList.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔎 Get AllowList
  ========================================

  Pool Hooks:   0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE

  0x3A34637a41aB08519d30Fdb65344aBa8E9b2e994
  ========================================
  Pool Hooks:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE
  ========================================
  ```

  **4. (Optional): Check if a particular sender is allowlisted:**

  <GitHubCard title="IsAllowListed.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/allowlist/IsAllowListed.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">


  Your output should look something like this:

</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Attempt a transfer (expected failure)" number={8} depth={3}>
  This step attempts a token transfer and is expected to fail because you removed your sender address from the allowlist. Hooks are configured per token pool, per chain, although this does not attach hooks on any destination-chain pool.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourDeployerAddress \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Expected result: the send transaction reverts. You should see an error that includes `SenderNotAllowed(address)`.

  If this step does **not** fail as expected, make sure:

  - Hooks are attached (`GetAdvancedPoolHooks.s.sol` shows `POOL_HOOKS`).
  - Your sender address is **NOT** on the allowlist (previous step returns NOT allowlisted).
  - The token pool is an authorized caller on the hooks (`GetAuthorizedCallers.s.sol` includes `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL`).
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Send a transfer again (expected success)" number={10} depth={3}>
  With hooks detached, the token pool returns to its default behavior and your transfer should succeed again.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourDeployerAddress \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Expected output (example):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0x3A34637a41aB08519d30Fdb65344aBa8E9b2e994 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```
</AnchoredAccordion>

# Set advanced pool hooks using Hardhat
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-advanced-pool-hooks-hardhat
Last Updated: 2026-05-05

<PageTabs
  pages={[

  },
]}
/>

CCIP v2 token pools support an optional [`AdvancedPoolHooks`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/pools/AdvancedPoolHooks.sol) contract being attached to them. \

## Before You Begin

## Tutorial

<AnchoredAccordion title="Review current pool hooks state" number={2} depth={3}>
  Use the `getAdvancedPoolHooks` task to check whether an `AdvancedPoolHooks` contract is currently attached to your token pool.

  <GitHubCard title="getAdvancedPoolHooks.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/configure/allowlist/getAdvancedPoolHooks.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the hooks query task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getAdvancedPoolHooks --network sepolia
  ```

  Example output (no hooks attached):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🪝 Get Advanced Pool Hooks
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View pool hooks
  ========================================

  No AdvancedPoolHooks contract is attached to this pool.
     Deploy one with:  npx hardhat deployAdvancedPoolHooks
     Attach it with:   npx hardhat updateAdvancedPoolHooks --newhook <address>

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  <Aside type="note">
    1. <code>getAdvancedPoolHooks()</code> is only available on TokenPool v2.0 and later. 2. If your token pool already
       has hooks attached, you can detach them by following the 'Detach hooks' section, to follow the tutorial.
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Deploy AdvancedPoolHooks" number={4} depth={3}>
  Use the `deployAdvancedPoolHooks` task to deploy a new hooks contract.

  <GitHubCard title="deployAdvancedPoolHooks.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/configure/allowlist/deployAdvancedPoolHooks.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the hooks deployment task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  Deployment flags:

  - `--allowlist`: CSV list of original outbound sender addresses allowed to initiate outbound transfers.
  - `--authorizedcallers`: CSV list of token pool addresses permitted to invoke the hooks.

  <Aside type="caution" title="Allowlist enablement is permanent">
    <ol>
      <li>
        Allowlist mode is set at deployment time and <strong>cannot be changed later</strong>.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you deploy with a non-empty <code>--allowlist</code>, the allowlist is permanently enabled.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you deploy with an empty allowlist, calling <code>applyAllowListUpdates()</code> later will revert with{" "}
        <code>AllowListNotEnabled()</code>.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  In this example, you will deploy hooks on Ethereum Sepolia with your deployer address on the allowlist, and authorize your token pool as a caller:

  <Aside type="note" title="Why we start by allowlisting the deployer">
    1. You will first allowlist your deployer address so you can attach hooks without immediately blocking your own
       transfers. 2. Later in the tutorial, you will remove your address from the allowlist to demonstrate an enforced
       failure.
  </Aside>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat deployAdvancedPoolHooks \
    --allowlist 0xYourDeployerAddress \
    --authorizedcallers $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔒 Deploy Advanced Pool Hooks
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Action:       Deploy pool hooks
  ========================================

  Advanced Pool Hooks Parameters:
    Allowlist Enabled:           Yes
    Allowlist Size:              1
      [0] 0x3A34637a41aB08519d30Fdb65344aBa8E9b2e994
    Threshold Amount:            Disabled (0)
    Policy Engine:               Disabled (0x0)
    Authorized Callers Enabled:  Yes
    Authorized Callers Size:     1
      [0] 0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9

  [Step 1] Deploying AdvancedPoolHooks on Ethereum Sepolia
  ⏳ Deployment tx: 0x9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d
  ✅ AdvancedPoolHooks deployed successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Deployment Complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  AdvancedPoolHooks Address: 0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE
  https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0xA11c0FFeE0bAdA55CAfEBaBeDeaDBeEfF00DBABE

  Deployment saved: deployments/advanced-pool-hooks/ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA/1746652800-AdvancedPoolHooks.json

  Configuration Summary:
    Allowlist:          Enabled
    Threshold:          Disabled
    Policy Engine:      Disabled
    Authorized Callers: Enabled

  Next Steps:
    1. When deploying a TokenPool, pass this hooks address as the 'poolHooks' parameter
    2. Attach to an existing pool: npx hardhat updateAdvancedPoolHooks --newhook <address> --network <network>
    3. Manage allowlist: npx hardhat updateAllowList --poolhooks <address> --add "0xAddr" --network <network>
  ========================================
  ```

  Export the hooks address for subsequent commands:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export POOL_HOOKS=0xHooksAddress
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Deployment address recovery">
    <ul>
      <li>
        Deployment addresses are saved to <code>deployments/advanced-pool-hooks/</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        If you lose the session export, retrieve the address from the JSON file under the <code>POOL_HOOKS</code> key.
      </li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Verify the setup" number={6} depth={3}>

  **1. Confirm hooks are attached to the pool:**


<AnchoredAccordion title="Attempt a transfer (expected failure)" number={8} depth={3}>
  This step attempts a token transfer and is expected to fail because you removed your sender address from the allowlist. Hooks are configured per token pool, per chain, although this does not attach hooks on any destination-chain pool.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourDeployerAddress \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Expected result: the send transaction reverts. You should see an error that includes `SenderNotAllowed(address)`.

  If this step does **not** fail as expected, make sure:

  - Hooks are attached (`getAdvancedPoolHooks` shows `POOL_HOOKS`).
  - Your sender address is **NOT** on the allowlist (previous step returns NOT allowlisted).
  - The token pool is an authorized caller on the hooks (`getAuthorizedCallers` includes `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL`).
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Send a transfer again (expected success)" number={10} depth={3}>
  With hooks detached, the token pool returns to its default behavior and your transfer should succeed again.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=1.23 \
    --receiver 0xYourDeployerAddress \
    --wallet hardhat:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Expected output (example):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Hardhat keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0x3A34637a41aB08519d30Fdb65344aBa8E9b2e994 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```
</AnchoredAccordion>

# Manage Token Transfer Fees Using Foundry
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-foundry
Last Updated: 2026-05-05

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

CCIP v2 token pools let pool owners opt into **pool-level token transfer fee overrides** per destination lane. When an override is disabled, the [OnRamp](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/onRamp/OnRamp.sol) falls back to [`FeeQuoter`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/FeeQuoter.sol) defaults for that lane. In this tutorial you will:

1. Review the current fee configuration for both configured lanes.
2. Optionally set a fee admin who can withdraw accrued fees.
3. Configure lane-specific flat fees, transfer fees, destination gas overhead, and destination bytes overhead.
4. Send a LINK-paid transfer and inspect accrued fees in the source token pool.
5. Withdraw accrued fee tokens.
6. Disable the fee configuration on both lanes to return to `FeeQuoter` defaults.

<Aside type="note" title="Defaults apply unless you opt in" />

## Before You Begin

## Tutorial

<Aside type="tip" title="Prerequisites">
  This tutorial assumes you have already deployed tokens and token pools on both chains. If not, complete one of the two
  tutorials first:

  Use the token pool address for the chain you are configuring. In a Burn & Mint setup, both pools are{" "}
  <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code> contracts. In a Lock & Mint setup, the source chain can use a{" "}
  <code>LockReleaseTokenPool</code> backed by an <code>ERC20LockBox</code>, while the destination chain uses a{" "}
  <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code>. This tutorial configures the token pool, not the lockbox.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN=0x...

  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  ```
</Aside>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Review Current Fee Configuration" number={2} depth={3}>
  Use `GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol` to read the current fee configuration for a destination lane from the source-chain token pool.

  <GitHubCard title="GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/fee-config/GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the fee config query script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  | Env var                   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                     |
  | ------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`DEST_CHAIN`</nobr> | Yes      | Remote chain whose lane is being queried.                                                                                                                       |
  | Source pool env var       | Yes      | `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL`, `ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL`, or the inline `TOKEN_POOL` alias for the source chain selected by `--rpc-url`. |

  1. Check the Ethereum Sepolia pool for the lane to Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/fee-config/GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 3478487238524512106

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                    false
    destGasOverhead:              0
    destBytesOverhead:            0
    finalityFeeUSDCents:          0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:      0
    finalityTransferFeeBps:       0
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:   0

  ⚠️  Fee config is disabled for this lane.
      The OnRamp will fall back to FeeQuoter defaults for this destination.

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  2. Check the Arbitrum Sepolia pool for the lane to Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA \
    forge script \
    script/configure/fee-config/GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Arbitrum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 16015286601757825753

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                    false
    destGasOverhead:              0
    destBytesOverhead:            0
    finalityFeeUSDCents:          0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:      0
    finalityTransferFeeBps:       0
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:   0

  ⚠️  Fee config is disabled for this lane.
      The OnRamp will fall back to FeeQuoter defaults for this destination.

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.arbiscan.io/address/0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  ========================================
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Fee config disabled by default">
    1. When fee config is disabled, the OnRamp uses FeeQuoter defaults for token transfer fee calculation on that source -> destination lane.
    2. If you have already configured fees, the script will show non-zero values and `isEnabled: true`.
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Verify the Updated Fee Configuration" number={4} depth={3}>
  Re-run `GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol` to confirm the final (Step 2) configuration for the Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia lane.

  1. Verify the Ethereum Sepolia pool for the lane to Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/fee-config/GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 3478487238524512106

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                    true
    destGasOverhead:              50000
    destBytesOverhead:            32
    finalityFeeUSDCents:          0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:      150
    finalityTransferFeeBps:       25
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:   0

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  2. Repeat for the reverse lane (Arbitrum Sepolia → Ethereum Sepolia):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA \
    forge script \
    script/configure/fee-config/GetTokenTransferFeeConfig.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL
  ```

  Success criteria:

  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `isEnabled: true`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `destGasOverhead: 50000`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `destBytesOverhead: 32`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `finalityFeeUSDCents: 0` and `finalityTransferFeeBps: 25`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `fastFinalityFeeUSDCents: 150` and `fastFinalityTransferFeeBps: 0`.
  - The reverse lane should show the same values after you repeat the two-step update.
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Inspect and Withdraw Accrued Fees" number={6} depth={3}>
  After the transfers complete, inspect the source pool balances again:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  FEE_TOKENS="$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    forge script \
    script/operations/GetFeeTokenBalances.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔍 Get Fee Token Balances
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Inspect fee token balances
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Fee Token Balances:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  ✅ 2 token(s) with non-zero balances are ready for withdrawal.
  ```

  Expected balances:

  - **Source token (bps fee)**: The default-finality send uses `finalityTransferFeeBps = 25`. With a `1.23` token transfer:
    - Retained by the pool: (1.23 \times 25 / 10000 = 0.003075) tokens
    - Verify in `ccip-cli` output: `tokenAmountBeforeTokenPoolFees (1.23)` - `tokens received (1.226925)` = `0.003075`
  - **LINK (fee token credited to the pool)**: The fee-token amount credited to the token pool is visible in the send output receipt where `receipts[i].issuer` equals the source token pool address. Sum `receipts[i].feeTokenAmount` across the default-finality and fast-finality sends, then convert from wei to LINK by dividing by (10^{18}). Confirm it matches `getFeeTokenBalances` for LINK.

  Set a value for the `FEE_ADMIN_KEYSTORE_NAME` variable inside your `.env`, using the instructions covered inside [Set Up Your Development Environment](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-foundry#set-up-your-development-environment).

  Use `WithdrawFeeTokens.s.sol` to withdraw accrued fee balances to a recipient. Withdraw as the configured fee admin:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  RECIPIENT=0xYourRecipientAddress \
    FEE_TOKENS="$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    forge script \
    script/operations/WithdrawFeeTokens.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $FEE_ADMIN_KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💸 Withdraw Fee Tokens
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Withdraw fee tokens
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Tokens to Withdraw:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  [Step 1] Withdrawing fee tokens on Ethereum Sepolia
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ✅ Fee tokens withdrawn successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Withdrawal complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  Recipient:    https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ========================================
  ```

  Or withdraw as the pool owner:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  RECIPIENT=0xYourRecipientAddress \
    FEE_TOKENS="$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    forge script \
    script/operations/WithdrawFeeTokens.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💸 Withdraw Fee Tokens
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Withdraw fee tokens
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Tokens to Withdraw:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  [Step 1] Withdrawing fee tokens on Ethereum Sepolia
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ✅ Fee tokens withdrawn successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Withdrawal complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  Recipient:    https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ========================================
  ```

  Verify the balances after withdrawal:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  FEE_TOKENS="$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    forge script \
    script/operations/GetFeeTokenBalances.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔍 Get Fee Token Balances
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Inspect fee token balances
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Fee Token Balances:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: 0 ⚠️  (skipping)
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 0 ⚠️  (skipping)

  ℹ️  No fee tokens have a non-zero balance in the pool. Nothing to withdraw.
  ========================================
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="ERC20 fee tokens only">
    <ul>
      <li>
        <code>WithdrawFeeTokens.s.sol</code> accepts ERC20 token addresses. It does not withdraw native gas tokens.
      </li>

      <li>
        This tutorial uses LINK for the fee-token portion so the accrued flat fee component can be inspected and withdrawn
        with the existing script.
      </li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<Aside type="caution" title="Troubleshooting">
  <ul>
    <li>
      <strong>Owner revert:</strong> confirm <code>KEYSTORE_NAME</code> is the owner of the source-chain token pool.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Fee admin withdrawal revert:</strong> confirm the fee admin was set, the correct fee admin keystore is
      used, and the action is withdrawal rather than owner-only configuration.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Missing gas:</strong> confirm the broadcaster has native gas on the source chain.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Missing LINK:</strong> confirm the sender has source-chain LINK when using <code>--fee-token LINK</code>.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Missing lane:</strong> confirm the pool lane was configured with <code>ApplyChainUpdates.s.sol</code>.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Wrong lane or pool:</strong> confirm <code>--rpc-url</code>, <code>DEST_CHAIN</code>, and the source pool
      env var match the intended source -> destination lane.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Invalid config:</strong> confirm <code>DEST_GAS_OVERHEAD</code> is not <code>0</code>,{" "}
      <code>DEST_BYTES_OVERHEAD</code> is at least <code>32</code>, and basis points values are below <code>10000</code>.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>Fast-finality revert:</strong> confirm the pool allows block-depth finality and the requested{" "}
      <code>finality=\<N></code> is not below the pool minimum.
    </li>

    <li>
      <strong>No accrued fees:</strong> confirm <code>FEE_TOKENS</code> includes LINK and the source token, the send
      completed, native fee token was not used, and flat or basis points fee values are non-zero.
    </li>
  </ul>
</Aside>

  demonstrate how to interact with Chainlink's systems, products, and services to integrate them into your own. This

# Manage Token Transfer Fees Using Hardhat
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-hardhat
Last Updated: 2026-05-05

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

CCIP v2 token pools let pool owners opt into **pool-level token transfer fee overrides** per destination lane. When an override is disabled, the [OnRamp](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/onRamp/OnRamp.sol) falls back to [`FeeQuoter`](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip/tree/contracts-ccip-v2.0.0/chains/evm/contracts/FeeQuoter.sol) defaults for that lane. In this tutorial you will:

1. Review the current fee configuration for both configured lanes.
2. Optionally set a fee admin who can withdraw accrued fees.
3. Configure lane-specific flat fees, transfer fees, destination gas overhead, and destination bytes overhead.
4. Send a LINK-paid transfer and inspect accrued fees in the source token pool.
5. Withdraw accrued fee tokens.
6. Disable the fee configuration on both lanes to return to `FeeQuoter` defaults.

<Aside type="note" title="Defaults apply unless you opt in" />

## Before You Begin

## Tutorial

<Aside type="tip" title="Prerequisites">
  This tutorial assumes you have already deployed tokens and token pools on both chains. If not, complete one of the two
  tutorials first:

  Use the token pool address for the chain you are configuring. In a Burn & Mint setup, both pools are{" "}
  <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code> contracts. In a Lock & Mint setup, the source chain can use a{" "}
  <code>LockReleaseTokenPool</code> backed by an <code>ERC20LockBox</code>, while the destination chain uses a{" "}
  <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code>. This tutorial configures the token pool, not the lockbox.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=0x...
  export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=0x...

  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  export ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  ```
</Aside>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Review Current Fee Configuration" number={2} depth={3}>
  Use `getTokenTransferFeeConfig` to read the current fee configuration for a destination lane from the source-chain token pool.

  <GitHubCard title="getTokenTransferFeeConfig.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/configure/fee-config/getTokenTransferFeeConfig.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the fee config query task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  | Input                      | Required | Description                                                                                                                               |
  | -------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`--destchain`</nobr> | Yes      | Remote chain whose lane is being queried.                                                                                                 |
  | Source pool env var        | Yes      | `ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL`, `ARBITRUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL`, or the `--tokenpool` override for the source chain selected by `--network`. |

  1. Check the Ethereum Sepolia pool for the lane to Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getTokenTransferFeeConfig \
    --destchain arbitrumSepolia \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 3478487238524512106

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                   false
    destGasOverhead:             0
    destBytesOverhead:           0
    finalityFeeUSDCents:         0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:     0
    finalityTransferFeeBps:      0
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:  0

  ⚠️  Fee config is disabled for this lane.
     The OnRamp will fall back to FeeQuoter defaults for this destination.

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  2. Check the Arbitrum Sepolia pool for the lane to Ethereum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getTokenTransferFeeConfig \
    --destchain sepolia \
    --network arbitrumSepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Arbitrum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 16015286601757825753

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                   false
    destGasOverhead:             0
    destBytesOverhead:           0
    finalityFeeUSDCents:         0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:     0
    finalityTransferFeeBps:      0
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:  0

  ⚠️  Fee config is disabled for this lane.
     The OnRamp will fall back to FeeQuoter defaults for this destination.

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.arbiscan.io/address/0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  ========================================
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Fee config disabled by default">
    1. When fee config is disabled, the OnRamp uses FeeQuoter defaults for token transfer fee calculation on that source -> destination lane.
    2. If you have already configured fees, the task will show non-zero values and `isEnabled: true`.
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Verify the Updated Fee Configuration" number={4} depth={3}>
  Re-run `getTokenTransferFeeConfig` to confirm the final (Step 2) configuration for the Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia lane.

  1. Verify the Ethereum Sepolia pool for the lane to Arbitrum Sepolia:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getTokenTransferFeeConfig \
    --destchain arbitrumSepolia \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💰 Get Token Transfer Fee Config
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       View fee config
  ========================================

  Dest Chain Selector: 3478487238524512106

  Fee Configuration:
    isEnabled:                   true
    destGasOverhead:             50000
    destBytesOverhead:           32
    finalityFeeUSDCents:         0
    fastFinalityFeeUSDCents:     150
    finalityTransferFeeBps:      25
    fastFinalityTransferFeeBps:  0

  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  2. Repeat for the reverse lane (Arbitrum Sepolia → Ethereum Sepolia):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getTokenTransferFeeConfig \
    --destchain sepolia \
    --network arbitrumSepolia
  ```

  Success criteria:

  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `isEnabled: true`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `destGasOverhead: 50000`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `destBytesOverhead: 32`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `finalityFeeUSDCents: 0` and `finalityTransferFeeBps: 25`.
  - Ethereum Sepolia → Arbitrum Sepolia shows `fastFinalityFeeUSDCents: 150` and `fastFinalityTransferFeeBps: 0`.
  - The reverse lane should show the same values after you repeat the two-step update.
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Inspect and Withdraw Accrued Fees" number={6} depth={3}>
  After the transfers complete, inspect the source pool balances again:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getFeeTokenBalances \
    --feetokens "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔍 Get Fee Token Balances
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Inspect fee token balances
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Fee Token Balances:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  ✅ 2 token(s) with non-zero balances are ready for withdrawal.

  To withdraw, run:
    npx hardhat withdrawFeeTokens --feetokens "0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789,0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09" --network sepolia
    (Add --recipient 0x... to send to a different address; defaults to the deployer wallet.)
  ========================================
  ```

  Expected balances:

  - **Source token (bps fee)**: The default-finality send uses `finalityTransferFeeBps = 25`. With a `1.23` token transfer:
    - Retained by the pool: (1.23 \times 25 / 10000 = 0.003075) tokens
    - Verify in `ccip-cli` output: `tokenAmountBeforeTokenPoolFees (1.23)` - `tokens received (1.226925)` = `0.003075`
  - **LINK (fee token credited to the pool)**: The fee-token amount credited to the token pool is visible in the send output receipt where `receipts[i].issuer` equals the source token pool address. Sum `receipts[i].feeTokenAmount` across the default-finality and fast-finality sends, then convert from wei to LINK by dividing by (10^{18}). Confirm it matches `getFeeTokenBalances` for LINK.

  Set a value for the `FEE_ADMIN_KEYSTORE_NAME` variable inside your `.env`, using the instructions covered inside [Set Up Your Development Environment](/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/set-transfer-fee-config-hardhat#set-up-your-development-environment).

  Use `withdrawFeeTokens` to withdraw accrued fee balances to a recipient. Withdraw as the configured fee admin:

  <GitHubCard title="withdrawFeeTokens.ts" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-hardhat/blob/main/tasks/operations/withdrawFeeTokens.ts" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the fee-token withdrawal task on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  KEYSTORE_NAME=$FEE_ADMIN_KEYSTORE_NAME \
    npx hardhat withdrawFeeTokens \
    --recipient 0xYourRecipientAddress \
    --feetokens "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💸 Withdraw Fee Tokens
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Withdraw fee tokens
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411

  Tokens to Withdraw:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  [Step 1] Withdrawing fee tokens on Ethereum Sepolia
  ⏳ Tx: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x5e1c0d9a8b7f6e5d4c3b2a190f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0a9b8c7d6
  ✅ Fee tokens withdrawn successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Withdrawal complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Recipient:    https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ========================================
  ```

  Or withdraw as the pool owner:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat withdrawFeeTokens \
    --recipient 0xYourRecipientAddress \
    --feetokens "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  💸 Withdraw Fee Tokens
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Withdraw fee tokens
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)
  Recipient:    0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411

  Tokens to Withdraw:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: <LINK_BALANCE_WEI>
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 3075000000000000

  [Step 1] Withdrawing fee tokens on Ethereum Sepolia
  ⏳ Tx: https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d
  ✅ Fee tokens withdrawn successfully!

  ========================================
  ✅ Withdrawal complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Recipient:    https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x368b6c4218Cd5B8feF04eFDb207Bd52f0566c411
  ========================================
  ```

  Verify the balances after withdrawal:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  npx hardhat getFeeTokenBalances \
    --feetokens "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_LINK,$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN" \
    --network sepolia
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  🔍 Get Fee Token Balances
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Inspect fee token balances
  ========================================

  Pool Token:   0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09 (for reference)

  Fee Token Balances:
    [0] 0x779877A7B0D9E8603169DdbD7836e478b4624789  →  balance: 0 ⚠️  (skipping)
    [1] 0xD73D06d36cEa36817186779fF877e418Ab759F09  →  balance: 0 ⚠️  (skipping)
  ```

    <ul>
      <li>`withdrawFeeTokens` accepts ERC20 token addresses. It does not withdraw native gas tokens.</li>

      <li>
        This tutorial uses LINK for the fee-token portion so the accrued flat fee component can be inspected and withdrawn
        with the existing task.
      </li>
    </ul>
  </Aside>
</AnchoredAccordion>

<Aside type="caution" title="Troubleshooting">

# Set Token Pool Rate Limits Using Foundry
Source: https://docs.chain.link/ccip/v2/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/update-rate-limiters-foundry
Last Updated: 2026-04-27

<PageTabs
  pages={[
  {
    name: "Foundry",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/update-rate-limiters-foundry",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/foundry-icn.png",
  },
  {
    name: "Hardhat",
    url: "/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/update-rate-limiters-hardhat",
    icon: "/images/tutorial-icons/hardhat-icn.png",
  },
]}
/>

In this tutorial you will:

1. Review current standard rate limiter configurations for your deployed token pool.
2. Update outbound and inbound standard rate limiter configurations.
3. Verify the updated configurations.
4. Test standard rate limiter enforcement with a cross-chain token transfer.
5. Optionally configure and test rate limits for faster than finality transfers.

## Before You Begin

## Tutorial

<Aside type="tip" title="Prerequisites">
  This tutorial assumes you have already deployed tokens and token pools on both chains. If not, complete one of the
  registration tutorials first:

  <ul>
    <li>
      <a href="/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry">Burn & Mint</a>
    </li>

    <li>
      <a href="/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry">Lock & Mint</a>
    </li>
  </ul>

  Make sure your token and token pool addresses are exported as environment variables:

  ```bash
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN=0x...

  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_TOKEN_POOL=0x...
  ```

  <br />

  This tutorial supports both CCT registration models:

  <ul>
    <li>
      In the Burn & Mint model, rate limiters are configured on the <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code> on each chain.
    </li>

    <li>
      In the Lock & Mint model, rate limiters are configured on the token pools: the source-chain{" "}
      <code>LockReleaseTokenPool</code> and the destination-chain <code>BurnMintTokenPool</code>. The{" "}
      <code>ERC20LockBox</code> is not rate-limited and is not updated by the scripts in this tutorial.
    </li>
  </ul>
</Aside>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Update Rate Limiter Configurations" number={2} depth={3}>
  Use the `UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol` script to update rate limiter configurations for an existing lane in your token pool. The direction to update is inferred automatically from whichever `OUTBOUND_*` / `INBOUND_*` environment variables you set.

  Only the directions you specify are updated; any direction you don't specify is left unchanged. Outbound and inbound are relative to the pool you're configuring:

  1. `outbound` is tokens leaving this pool toward `DEST_CHAIN`;
  2. `inbound` is tokens arriving from `DEST_CHAIN` into this pool.

  <Aside type="note" title="Lane must exist">
    <ol>
      <li>Rate limiters can only be updated for lanes that already exist.</li>

      <li>
        If you haven't configured the lane yet, complete one of the two tutorials first:

        <ul>
          <li>
            <a href="/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-burn-mint-foundry">Burn & Mint</a>
          </li>

          <li>
            <a href="/ccip/evm/tutorials/cross-chain-tokens/register-from-eoa-lock-mint-foundry">Lock & Mint</a>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </li>

      <li>
        Run <code>ApplyChainUpdates.s.sol</code> to configure the lane.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  <GitHubCard title="UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol" href="https://github.com/smartcontractkit/docs-cct-foundry/blob/main/script/configure/rate-limiter/UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol" iconName="github-svg-card">
    View the rate limiter update script on GitHub.
  </GitHubCard>

  | <nobr>Env var</nobr>                        | <nobr>Required</nobr>           | <nobr>Description</nobr>                                                                                                          |
  | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | <nobr>`DEST_CHAIN`</nobr>                   | <nobr>Yes</nobr>                | <nobr>Remote chain whose lane is being updated</nobr>                                                                             |
  | <nobr>`OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY`</nobr> | <nobr>To update outbound</nobr> | <nobr>Token bucket capacity for outbound transfers</nobr>                                                                         |
  | <nobr>`OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE`</nobr>     | <nobr>To update outbound</nobr> | <nobr>Token bucket refill rate (tokens/second) for outbound transfers</nobr>                                                      |
  | <nobr>`OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED`</nobr>  | <nobr>No</nobr>                 | <nobr>Override `isEnabled` explicitly (`true`/`false`; defaults to `true` when CAPACITY or RATE are set)</nobr>                   |
  | <nobr>`INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY`</nobr>  | <nobr>To update inbound</nobr>  | <nobr>Token bucket capacity for inbound transfers</nobr>                                                                          |
  | <nobr>`INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE`</nobr>      | <nobr>To update inbound</nobr>  | <nobr>Token bucket refill rate (tokens/second) for inbound transfers</nobr>                                                       |
  | <nobr>`INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED`</nobr>   | <nobr>No</nobr>                 | <nobr>Override `isEnabled` explicitly (`true`/`false`; defaults to `true` when CAPACITY or RATE are set)</nobr>                   |
  | <nobr>`FAST_FINALITY`</nobr>                | <nobr>No</nobr>                 | <nobr>`true` to update the faster than finality bucket instead of the standard finality bucket (v2 only, default: `false`)</nobr> |

  <Aside type="note" title="Access control and compatibility">
    <ol>
      <li>
        The pool owner and the designated <code>rateLimitAdmin</code> can update rate limiters.
      </li>

      <li>
        The <code>rateLimitAdmin</code> is configured via <code>SetDynamicConfig.s.sol</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        This script supports both v1 and v2 token pools: on v2 pools it calls <code>setRateLimitConfig()</code>; on v1
        pools it falls back to <code>setChainRateLimiterConfig()</code>.
      </li>

      <li>
        The <code>FAST_FINALITY</code> flag is v2-only and is ignored on v1 pools.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  <Aside type="note" title="Configuration best practices">
    <ol>
      <li>
        Set inbound rate limits a bit higher than outbound limits on the same lane. Many chains finalize blocks in
        batches, so multiple outbound messages may become executable on the destination simultaneously, requiring slightly
        more inbound capacity.
      </li>

      <li>
        The exact additional capacity required depends on the refill rate and the size of the source chain epochs and CCIP
        round time. In most cases, a 5-10% buffer should be sufficient.
      </li>

      <li>
        <code>rate</code> must be less than or equal to <code>capacity</code>, and when disabling rate limiting (
        <code>isEnabled: false</code>), both <code>capacity</code> and <code>rate</code> must be <code>0</code>.
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  In this example, we configure an 18-decimal token with outbound capacity of 10 tokens (refilling at 0.1 tokens/sec) and inbound capacity of 11 tokens (refilling at 0.11 tokens/sec, a 10% buffer):

  1. Update the Ethereum Sepolia pool (lane to Arbitrum Sepolia):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=10000000000000000000 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=11000000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=110000000000000000 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/rate-limiter/UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  ⚡️ Update Rate Limiters
  ========================================
  Chain:        Ethereum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Arbitrum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Action:       Update rate limits
  Direction:    Outbound + Inbound
  Bucket:       Standard finality
  ========================================

  Pool Version: v2 (setRateLimitConfig)

  Current Rate Limiter State:
  Outbound Enabled:  false
  Outbound Capacity: 0
  Outbound Rate:     0
  Outbound Tokens:   0
  Inbound  Enabled:  false
  Inbound  Capacity: 0
  Inbound  Rate:     0
  Inbound  Tokens:   0

  New Configuration:
  Outbound Enabled:  true
  Outbound Capacity: 10000000000000000000
  Outbound Rate:     100000000000000000
  Inbound Enabled:   true
  Inbound Capacity:  11000000000000000000
  Inbound Rate:      110000000000000000

  ========================================
  ✅ Rate limiter update complete on Ethereum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/0x147D4625b71f58D7CFA54BB705DC7741B94e0CE9
  ========================================
  ```

  2. Update the Arbitrum Sepolia pool (lane to Ethereum Sepolia):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=10000000000000000000 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=100000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY=11000000000000000000 \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_RATE=110000000000000000 \
    forge script \
    script/configure/rate-limiter/UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ========================================
  ⚡️ Update Rate Limiters
  ========================================
  Chain:        Arbitrum Sepolia
  Remote Chain: Ethereum Sepolia
  Token Pool:   0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  Action:       Update rate limits
  Direction:    Outbound + Inbound
  Bucket:       Standard finality
  ========================================

  Pool Version: v2 (setRateLimitConfig)

  Current Rate Limiter State:
  Outbound Enabled:  false
  Outbound Capacity: 0
  Outbound Rate:     0
  Outbound Tokens:   0
  Inbound  Enabled:  false
  Inbound  Capacity: 0
  Inbound  Rate:     0
  Inbound  Tokens:   0

  New Configuration:
  Outbound Enabled:  true
  Outbound Capacity: 10000000000000000000
  Outbound Rate:     100000000000000000
  Inbound Enabled:   true
  Inbound Capacity:  11000000000000000000
  Inbound Rate:      110000000000000000

  ========================================
  ✅ Rate limiter update complete on Arbitrum Sepolia!
  ========================================
  Token Pool:   0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  Token Pool:   https://sepolia.arbiscan.io/address/0x7D2f4A6c8E1b3D5a9F0c2E4b6A8d1C3e5F7a9B2d
  ========================================
  ```

  3. To **Disable** rate limiters for a lane, set `OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false` and `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false`:

  <Aside type="caution" title="Disabling rate limiters">
    <ol>
      <li>
        We highly recommend that devs have at least some limits set up. We advise against completely disabling rate
        limiters unless absolutely necessary.
      </li>

      <li>
        <strong>Informational-only for this tutorial:</strong> If you disable rate limiters here, the later{" "}
        <strong>Test the Rate Limiter Configurations</strong> section will not behave as described (it will not revert
        with <code>TokenMaxCapacityExceeded</code> / <code>TokenRateLimitReached</code>).
      </li>
    </ol>
  </Aside>

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  DEST_CHAIN=ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1 \
    OUTBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false \
    INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false \
    forge script \
    script/configure/rate-limiter/UpdateRateLimiters.s.sol \
    --rpc-url $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL \
    --account $KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --broadcast
  ```
</AnchoredAccordion>

<AnchoredAccordion title="Test the Rate Limiter Configurations" number={4} depth={3}>
  Initiate a cross-chain transfer to verify that the rate limiter enforces the configured limits.

  <Aside type="note" title="Token balance">
    Ensure your EOA has a sufficient balance of the cross-chain token on the source chain. If you need more tokens, use
    the <code>MintTokens.s.sol</code> script or transfer tokens from another account.
  </Aside>

  Before testing, export the router and token addresses for the source chain:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER=0x...
  export ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=0x...
  ```

  <Aside type="note" title="Router address">
    You can find the router address for your chain in the [CCIP
    Directory](https://docs.chain.link/ccip/directory/testnet).
  </Aside>

  > **Note:**
  >
  > 1. Add `--fee-token LINK` to pay CCIP fees in LINK. If you omit this flag, fees are paid in the native gas token.
  > 2. Use `--receiver <address>` for a custom recipient. If omitted on EVM-to-EVM, the receiver defaults to the sender.

  #### Test 1: Exceed capacity

  Transfer one wei more than the outbound capacity (10 tokens + 1 wei). This should fail because the requested amount exceeds the bucket size.

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=10.000000000000000001 \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  error: Failed to call "ccipSend"
  Error = execution reverted: TokenMaxCapacityExceeded(uint256 capacity, uint256 requested, address tokenAddress)
  Revert.error = TokenMaxCapacityExceeded(uint256,uint256,address)
  Revert.capacity = 10000000000000000000n
  Revert.requested = 10000000000000000001n
  Revert.tokenAddress = 0x9602399103Ff5F87587Ac5A28E1551A0bA0c6C0D
  ```

  The transfer should fail with `TokenMaxCapacityExceeded` because the requested amount is larger than the bucket capacity.

  <Aside type="note" title="How does the token bucket work?">
    CCIP rate limiters use a <em>token bucket</em> model. Think of the bucket as a virtual allowance that controls how
    many tokens can flow through the pool in a given window:

    <ol>
      <li>
        The bucket starts full at its configured <strong>capacity</strong>.
      </li>

      <li>
        Each transfer <strong>consumes</strong> its amount from the bucket.
      </li>

      <li>
        The bucket <strong>refills</strong> continuously at the configured <strong>rate</strong> (tokens per second).
      </li>
    </ol>

    In this tutorial, the outbound bucket has a capacity of 10 tokens and refills at 0.1 tokens/sec. Transferring all 10
    tokens in one go "drains" the bucket to zero. Any immediate follow-up transfer will fail because the bucket needs 100
    seconds (10 ÷ 0.1) to fully replenish.
  </Aside>

  #### Test 2: Drain the bucket, then hit the rate

  1. **First transfer** (succeeds: drains the outbound bucket):

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=10 \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  🚀 Sending message to 0xE23Fc63F47F08F58B9d7448d4CCE0bCDcc96d7F3 @ ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 , tx => 0x3dc40bea29f3e3fc93ff8fce0dda45fd7f55a07ace5089646e018874c8b6745e , messageId => 0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  CCIP Explorer: https://ccip.chain.link/msg/0x4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293
  ```

  2. **Second transfer** (fails: bucket has not refilled):

  Run the same command immediately:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  ccip-cli send \
    --source ethereum-testnet-sepolia \
    --router $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_ROUTER \
    --dest ethereum-testnet-sepolia-arbitrum-1 \
    --transfer-tokens $ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_TOKEN=10 \
    --wallet foundry:$KEYSTORE_NAME \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL" \
    --rpc "$ETHEREUM_TESTNET_SEPOLIA_ARBITRUM_1_RPC_URL"
  ```

  Your output should look something like this:

  ```bash filename="Terminal"
  Fee: 130129888907619n = 0.000130129888907619 ETH
  ✔ Enter password for Foundry keystore 'PRIVATE_KEY'
  error: Failed to call "ccipSend"
  Error = execution reverted: TokenRateLimitReached(uint256 minWaitInSeconds, uint256 available, address tokenAddress)
  Revert.error = TokenRateLimitReached(uint256,uint256,address)
  Revert.minWaitInSeconds = 100n
  Revert.available = 0n
  Revert.tokenAddress = 0x9602399103Ff5F87587Ac5A28E1551A0bA0c6C0D
  ```

  The transfer should fail with `TokenRateLimitReached` because the bucket has not yet refilled. With a capacity of 10 tokens and a rate of 0.1 tokens per second, it takes 100 seconds to fully replenish.
</AnchoredAccordion>

  This page includes an educational example to use a Chainlink system, product, or service and is provided to
